pointers.sentence: The changes from Django 5.0 to this commit in `django.forms` and `django/core/validators.py`: the div layout as the default, `RenderableFieldMixin.as_field_group`, `bound_field_class`, the ARIA attributes, the URL field's `"https"`, the blank choice's label, and `EmailValidator`'s new methods.

Since 5.0 a form draws itself as divisions: `BaseRenderer.form_template_name` is `"django/forms/div.html"` and `BaseRenderer.formset_template_name` `"django/forms/formsets/div.html"`, and `str(form)` renders the renderer's (`django/forms/renderers.py:BaseRenderer`, `django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.template_name`).

Since 5.0 a form draws itself as divisions: `BaseRenderer.form_template_name` is `"django/forms/div.html"` and `BaseRenderer.formset_template_name` `"django/forms/formsets/div.html"`, and `str(form)` renders the renderer's (`django/forms/renderers.py:BaseRenderer`, `django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.template_name`).

It prints `{{ field.as_field_group }}`, and `RenderableFieldMixin.as_field_group` renders the bound field's template, which draws label, help text, errors and widget (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableFieldMixin.as_field_group`).

That template is one given to the form field as `template_name=`, or else the renderer's `BaseRenderer.field_template_name`, `"django/forms/field.html"` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.template_name`).

`BaseForm.get_context` hands the template each field's `ErrorList` as it is, and the template escapes a plain string (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.get_context`): in a run, an error class whose `__str__` returned `"…"` unmarked drew `<b>`.
Django's own error lists are marked safe by `RenderableMixin.render` (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableMixin.render`).
Before 5.2 a field had bound fields of another class only by an override of `Field.get_bound_field` (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.get_bound_field`).

The form's is settled by `BaseForm.__init__`: its argument, else its class's `BaseForm.bound_field_class`, else the renderer's `BaseRenderer.bound_field_class`, `None` on Django's renderers (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__init__`).

At this commit `BoundField.aria_describedby` (5.2) joins `BoundField.auto_id` with `"_helptext"` and `"_error"`, as the field has help text and errors (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.aria_describedby`).

`BoundField.build_widget_attrs` puts it on the widget unless the widget has its own or asks for a fieldset; then `"django/forms/field.html"` puts it on the fieldset (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`).

The errors' id is written by `"django/forms/errors/list/ul.html"` from `ErrorList.field_id` (5.2), which `BaseForm.add_error` sets to the field's `auto_id` (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.add_error`).

In 5.0 the scheme `URLField.to_python` puts in front of a value that has none became `URLField.assume_scheme`, an argument whose default, `"http"`, was deprecated at once; in 6.0 the default became `"https"`, and FORMS_URLFIELD_ASSUME_HTTPS, the transitional setting that took it early, was removed (`django/forms/fields.py:URLField.__init__`).

Since 6.1 its label comes from `get_blank_choice_label`: `BLANK_CHOICE_LABEL`, a translated `"- Select an option -"`, or the dashes of `BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` while `USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` is true (`django/db/models/utils.py:get_blank_choice_label`).

Defining the setting warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`); in a run, reading the constant did not ([Choices: `ChoiceField`, `ModelChoiceField` and the choice widgets](../forms/choices.md#the-blank-choices-label)).

Now the call is `EmailValidator.parse_address`, then `EmailValidator.validate`, which hands the user part to `EmailValidator.validate_username` and the domain to `EmailValidator.validate_domain`; each raises `ValidationError` itself, with the part as the parameter `"username"` or `"domain"` beside `"value"` (`django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.validate`).

The old method is deprecated, to go in Django 2029: a subclass that defines it warns with `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` as the class is made, and `validate` then calls it in place of `validate_domain` (`django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.__init_subclass__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md#domain-names-urls-and-email-addresses)).

The old method is deprecated, to go in Django 2029: a subclass that defines it warns with `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` as the class is made, and `validate` then calls it in place of `validate_domain` (`django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.__init_subclass__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md#domain-names-urls-and-email-addresses)).
